# Week 3: Homework

## Task:

1.  SSPs: shared socioeconomic pathways
    1.  SSP1: lots of mitigation and adaptation
    2.  SSP5: fossil fuel development
2.  Pick any country in the world and:
    1.  produce descriptive statistics that show:
        1.  the difference in **maximum temperature** for key cities between SSP1 and SSP5 for the years 2081-2100
        2.  use any model and resolution

## Data Sources:

- [WorldClim future projections](https://www.worldclim.org/data/cmip6/cmip6_clim2.5m.html)

- [Country outlines](https://gadm.org/data.html)

- [World city points](https://hub.arcgis.com/datasets/esri::world-cities/explore?location=3.049068%2C-178.464838%2C1.71)

## Outline:

1.  Load packages
2.  Load in data
    1.  shape/geom – usa
        1.  check CRS
        2.  print(\<dataframe\>)
    2.  load in climate data
        1.  use dplyr with str_detect() to search for file names contains tif
        2.  load data into a SpatRaster
        3.  rename layers within the stack
    3.  load city data
        1.  create data frame of key cities (if needed?)
        2.  Extract the data from the Rasterstack for all points using terra::extract – extract as a tibble, add_column
3.  Descriptive Statistics
    1.  crop then mask raster to shape/geom of usa
    2.  create a dual data histogram for city that shows max temp in ssp1 and ssp5
        1.  loop this for all key cities

## Load Packages

```{r}
library(sf) 
library(here)
library(tidyverse) 
library(terra) 
library(tidyterra)
library(janitor)
```

## Read in Vector Data

```{r}
# read in usa boundary & clean names
usa_outline <- st_read("gadm41_USA.gpkg", 
                      layer='ADM_ADM_0')

usa_outline <- clean_names(usa_outline)
#plot(usa_outline) 

usa_state <- st_read("gadm41_USA.gpkg", 
                     layer='ADM_ADM_1')

usa_state <- clean_names(usa_state)
#plot(usa_state) 


# read in key city data: keeping only us cities & select columns
usa_city <- st_read("USA_Cities.geojson") %>%
  filter_out(FIPS_CNTRY != "US") %>%
  select(FID, OBJECTID, CITY_NAME, ADMIN_NAME, FIPS_CNTRY, CNTRY_NAME, STATUS)

usa_city <- clean_names(usa_city)


#check CRS
#print(usa_city)
#print(usa_outline)

```

```{r}
#select just the states that contain the key cities I want to focus on  
state_keep <- c("Connecticut", "District of Columbia", 	"Maine", "Maryland", "Massachusetts", "New Hampshire", "New York", "Pennsylvania", "Rhode Island", "Vermont")

usa_state<- usa_state %>%
  filter(name_1 %in% state_keep) %>%
  select(name_1, geom)

nrow(usa_state)
```

ssp5$Jan

## Loading City Data

1.  load city data
    1.  create data frame of key cities (if needed?)
    2.  Extract the data from the Rasterstack for all points using terra::extract – extract as a tibble, add_column

```{r}
#identify just key cities in the northeast to keep as our focus "key cities" 
#create new df with those and match them to extract new df from usa_city df

ne_city_keep <- c("Hartford", "Washington D.C.", "Augusta", "Baltimore", "Boston", "Concord", "New York", "Philadelphia", "Providence", "Montpelier")

ne_city <- usa_city %>%
 filter(city_name %in% ne_city_keep)
  
# Extract the data from the Rasterstack for all points 
us_city_temp_ssp1<- terra::extract(ssp1, ne_city) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  add_column(city_name = ne_city$city_name, .before = "Jan")

us_city_temp_ssp5 <- terra::extract(ssp5, ne_city) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  add_column(city_name = ne_city$city_name, .before = "Jan")
```

## Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
# CROP 
# SSP1
us_temp_ssp1 <- usa_state %>%
  # now crop our temp data to the extent
  terra::crop(ssp1,.)

# SSP5
us_temp_ssp5 <- usa_state %>%
  # now crop our temp data to the extent
  terra::crop(ssp5,.)
```

```{r}
# MASK
exact_us_temp_ssp1 <-terra::mask(us_temp_ssp1, usa_state)
exact_us_temp_ssp5 <-terra::mask(us_temp_ssp5, usa_state)

```

```{r}
par(family = "Futura")
library(tidyterra)
ggplot() +
  # function from tidyterra
  geom_spatraster(
    # the raster 
    data = exact_us_temp_ssp1,
    # the layer within the raster
    aes(fill = Mar)
  ) + geom_sf(data = ne_city)
  
```

## Creating Bar Chart

```{r}
# convert data to long data type 
squish_ssp1 <-us_city_temp_ssp1%>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Jan:Dec,
    names_to = "Month",
    values_to = "Temp"
  ) %>% add_column(scenario = "ssp1") #add column with the spp scenario to keep track 

head(squish_ssp1)

squish_ssp5 <-us_city_temp_ssp5%>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Jan:Dec,
    names_to = "Month",
    values_to = "Temp"
  ) %>% add_column(scenario = "ssp5") #add column with the spp scenario to keep track 

head(squish_ssp5)

#combine both of the long data frames into one stacked df
squish_ssp1_ssp5 <- bind_rows(squish_ssp1, squish_ssp5)
nrow(squish_ssp1_ssp5)


squish_ordered <- squish_ssp1_ssp5 %>%
  drop_na()%>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month))

nrow(squish_ordered) #check to make sure drop_na didnt remove anything 
```

```{r}
# create bar chart for each city

library(ggplot2)
  
ggplot(squish_ordered, aes(x= Month, y = Temp, fill= scenario)) +
  geom_bar(stat= "identity", position = "identity", alpha = 0.2) + 
  labs(title = "Average Maximum Temperature by Month for Key Cities in the NE", x = "Month", y = "Average Maximum Temperature (C)") +
  facet_wrap(city_name ~ .)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red"))


```

```{r}
# convert squish_ordered back to wide 
stretch_ordered <- squish_ordered %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = Temp) %>%
  mutate(diff = ssp5 - ssp1)


# diff in mean per year by city
mean_temp <- stretch_ordered %>%
  group_by(city_name) %>%
  summarise(mean_diff_temp = mean(diff, na.rm=TRUE))


```
